name: Pad Thai
description: Stir-fried rice noodles with egg, tofu, tamarind, fish sauce, dried shrimp, garlic and shallots, served with lime wedges, bean sprouts and often crushed peanuts; fresh shrimp, other seafood or meat may be added. Created in the mid-20th century, it has become one of Thailand's national dishes and a common street food.
how_to_eat: Squeeze over the lime and add chilli flakes, sugar or fish sauce from the table caddy to taste.
how_to_order: Ask for 'phat thai kung' (with shrimp) at street woks and night markets.

name: Tom Yum Goong
description: A hot and sour prawn soup flavoured with lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, chillies, fish sauce and lime juice. A Central Thai dish eaten all over the country, it comes clear (nam sai) or creamy (nam khon) and was inscribed by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage in 2024.
how_to_eat: Eat with steamed jasmine rice; the herbs are for flavour and are usually left aside.
how_to_order: Ask for 'tom yam kung', either 'nam sai' (clear) or 'nam khon' (creamy).

name: Green Curry
local_name: แกงเขียวหวาน
description: Kaeng khiao wan is a coconut-milk curry made with green chilli paste (which includes shrimp paste), fish sauce, palm sugar, Thai eggplants and basil, traditionally with fish, fish balls or meat. It originated in central Thailand in the early 20th century.
how_to_eat: Spoon over steamed jasmine rice or eat with khanom chin rice noodles.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kaeng khiao wan kai' (chicken) at curry-and-rice shops.

name: Pad Kaphrao
description: Meat such as pork, chicken or beef, or seafood, stir-fried with holy basil, garlic and bird's eye chilli and seasoned with soy sauce, fish sauce and sugar. It is one of the most popular dishes in Thailand, eaten with rice and optionally topped with a fried egg.
how_to_eat: Eat over rice, ideally with a crispy fried egg on top.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khao phat kaphrao mu' (pork) and add 'khai dao' for a fried egg.

name: Khao Man Kai
local_name: ข้าวมันไก่
description: Thailand's version of Hainanese chicken rice (the name means 'chicken oily rice'): poached chicken on rice cooked with chicken fat, served with cucumber, a bowl of clear chicken broth and a sauce of fermented soybean paste, thick soy sauce, chilli, ginger, garlic and vinegar.
how_to_eat: Pour the sauce over the chicken and sip the broth between bites.
how_to_order: Look for stalls with whole poached chickens hanging in the window.

name: Boat Noodles
local_name: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือ
description: Kuaitiao ruea are noodles with pork and beef in a strong, dark broth of dark soy sauce, pickled bean curd, cinnamon and spices, thickened with pig or cow blood. Once sold from boats on Bangkok's canals, they still come in small bowls.
how_to_eat: Order several small bowls and season with chilli, vinegar and sugar.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kuai tiao ruea' with 'mu' (pork) or 'nuea' (beef).

name: Mango Sticky Rice
local_name: ข้าวเหนียวมะม่วง
description: Khao niao mamuang is sticky rice cooked with sweetened, salted coconut milk and served with ripe mango, sometimes topped with roasted mung beans or toasted sesame seeds. A common Thai street dessert, it is mostly eaten in the peak mango season of April and May.
how_to_eat: Eat the mango and rice together, with extra coconut cream poured over.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khao niao mamuang' at dessert stalls and markets.

name: Thai Iced Tea
description: Cha yen is strongly brewed black tea sweetened with sugar and condensed milk, served over ice and topped with evaporated or whole milk. Street and market stalls sell it over crushed ice in plastic bags or tall plastic cups.
how_to_order: Ask for 'cha yen' at drink stalls; 'cha dam yen' is the version without milk.

name: Khao Soi
description: A curry-like coconut-milk noodle soup with boiled and crispy fried egg noodles, usually with chicken or beef. Often called Chiang Mai's most iconic dish, it came to northern Thailand with Chin Haw Muslim traders from Yunnan.
how_to_eat: Add the pickled mustard greens, shallots and lime served on the side.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khao soi kai' (chicken) at noodle shops in Chiang Mai.

name: Khanom Chin Nam Ngiao
local_name: ขนมจีนน้ำเงี้ยว
description: Fermented rice noodles (khanom chin) in a spicy, tangy pork or beef broth with tomatoes, blood cake and dried red cotton tree flowers, flavoured with thua nao fermented soybeans. Originally a Shan dish, it is a Lanna favourite served at banquets and special occasions.
how_to_eat: Eat with the fresh herbs, beansprouts and cabbage served alongside.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khanom chin nam ngiao' at northern noodle stalls.

name: Sai Ua
description: A grilled sausage of coarsely chopped fatty pork seasoned with lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, shallots, chillies, garlic, sticky rice and fish sauce. Originating in Laos, it is a staple of northern Thailand, where it is also called Chiang Mai sausage.
how_to_eat: Eat in slices with sticky rice and fresh vegetables.
how_to_order: Buy by the coil or slice at northern markets.

name: Nam Phrik Num
local_name: น้ำพริกหนุ่ม
description: A paste of pounded roasted large green chillies, shallots and garlic with coriander leaves, lime juice and fish sauce. Of Lao origin, it is a classic Northern Thai dip.
how_to_eat: Scoop with sticky rice, boiled vegetables or pork crackling (khaep mu).
how_to_order: Buy in bags at northern markets, often sold with pork crackling.

name: Kaeng Hang Le
description: A rich, Burmese-origin pork belly curry made with a paste including shrimp paste, a dried-spice masala, black soy sauce, fish sauce, ginger, pickled garlic and peanuts. It is a festive dish and a specialty of northern Thailand.
how_to_eat: Eat with steamed long-grain rice rather than sticky rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kaeng hang le' at northern curry shops.

name: Kaeng Khanun
description: A Northern Thai curry of young jackfruit, usually with pork, tomatoes and cha-om leaves, in a paste of dried chillies, shrimp paste, shallots, garlic, galangal and lemongrass. Its name is considered lucky, so it is cooked for the northern New Year and at weddings.
how_to_eat: Eat with sticky rice.
how_to_order: Look for it at northern rice-and-curry stalls.

name: Som Tam
description: Green papaya salad pounded in a mortar with chillies, lime, fish sauce and palm sugar; the Central Thai version adds peanuts and dried shrimp, while Isan versions use pickled crab or pla ra fermented fish. Believed to be of Lao origin, it spread through Thailand from Isan.
how_to_eat: Eat with sticky rice and grilled chicken.
how_to_order: Ask for 'som tam Thai' (milder, with peanuts) or 'som tam pu pla ra' (Isan style) and say how many chillies.

name: Larb
description: A spicy, sour salad of minced meat with lime, fish sauce, chillies, mint and toasted ground rice. Of Lao origin, it is eaten across Isan and northern Thailand.
how_to_eat: Eat with sticky rice and raw vegetables.
how_to_order: Ask for 'lap mu' (pork) or 'lap kai' (chicken) at Isan restaurants.

name: Kai Yang
description: Grilled chicken, often halved and flattened, marinated in fish sauce, garlic, turmeric, coriander root and white pepper. Shared by Lao and Thai cooking, it is a staple of street markets.
how_to_eat: Dip in jaew chilli sauce and eat with som tam and sticky rice.
how_to_order: Buy by the half or whole bird from charcoal grills.

name: Nam Tok
description: A spicy salad of sliced grilled pork or beef with lime, fish sauce, chillies, herbs and toasted rice powder. The name means 'waterfall', after the juices dripping from the grilling meat.
how_to_eat: Eat with sticky rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'mu nam tok' (pork) or 'nuea nam tok' (beef).

name: Sai Krok Isan
local_name: ไส้กรอกอีสาน
description: A sour fermented sausage of fatty pork and sticky rice with garlic, left to ferment for a few days before grilling. It originated in Isan.
how_to_eat: Eat with bird's eye chillies, raw cabbage and sliced ginger.
how_to_order: Buy grilled on skewers at markets and street grills.

name: Sticky Rice
local_name: ข้าวเหนียว
description: Glutinous rice, soaked and steamed, is the staple of Isan and northern Thailand. It is served in small woven baskets and eaten with almost every Isan meal.
how_to_eat: Roll a small ball with your fingers and use it to scoop up food.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khao niao'; it comes in small woven baskets.

name: Kaeng Tai Pla
description: A very spicy curry flavoured with tai pla, a salty sauce of fermented fish entrails, plus shrimp paste, turmeric, chillies and vegetables such as bamboo shoots and eggplant, usually with fish. It is a famous dish of Phatthalung Province, also found across the South.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice and plenty of fresh vegetables.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kaeng tai pla' at southern curry-and-rice shops.

name: Kaeng Lueang
description: The southern form of sour curry: a turmeric-yellow, sour and fiery curry without coconut milk, usually with fish and vegetables.
how_to_eat: Eat with steamed rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kaeng lueang pla' (with fish).

name: Khua Kling
description: A very spicy dry-fried curry of chopped meat (usually beef, chicken or pork) in a southern curry paste of dried chillies, black pepper, garlic, galangal, lemongrass, turmeric and shrimp paste, served with shredded kaffir lime leaves. It comes from Southern Thailand.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice and raw vegetables to cool the heat.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khua kling mu' (pork) or 'khua kling nuea' (beef).

name: Khao Yam
description: A Southern Thai rice salad of rice with toppings such as toasted coconut, pomelo, bean sprouts, lime leaves and dried shrimp, dressed with budu, a fermented fish sauce.
how_to_eat: Pour over the sauce and mix everything together before eating.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khao yam' at southern breakfast stalls and markets.

name: Massaman Curry
local_name: แกงมัสมั่น
description: A rich coconut-milk curry with potatoes, onions and peanuts, most often with chicken, whose paste combines dried spices such as cardamom, cinnamon and cloves with shrimp paste and lemongrass. Its name comes from the Persian word for 'Muslim', reflecting the dish's Muslim roots.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice or roti.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kaeng matsaman' with 'kai' (chicken) or 'nuea' (beef).
